source.local_path: user-supplied screen recording of a YouTube page
source.title: Two vertical shorts shown inside 'Yapay Zekayı Video Makinesine Çevirdim!' by @wpmavi

platform_metadata.description: The recording is of a YouTube watch page, not of the shorts themselves. The player window was cropped out and upscaled, so shot boundaries and layout are reliable while fine typography is not.

content_analysis.summary: Two vertical explainer shorts made by the same system. The first answers why a bird on a high-voltage line is not electrocuted: both feet sit at the same potential, so no current flows through it, and the danger only appears at a second contact with a different potential. The second walks through how an offshore wind farm is built and how its power reaches shore.
key_claims: A bird's two feet are on the same wire, so at the same electrical potential
Current follows a difference, not a voltage on its own
A second contact at a different potential - a pole, the ground - is what makes current flow
Undersea cables carry the farm's electricity to shore
content_analysis.target_audience: General Turkish-speaking audience on Shorts; curiosity-driven, no technical background assumed
content_analysis.hook_technique: A calm, familiar image with an implicit question written over it - a bird sitting on a line, and the line 'why isn't it electrocuted?'
content_analysis.call_to_action: None visible in the frames sampled

scenes.description: Birds crowded along a power line against a blue sky, shot from below. Chip top-left reads BİNLERCE VOLT.
scenes.on_screen_text: BİNLERCE VOLT / 'Binlerce voltluk telde sakin bir kuş. Neden çarpılmıyor?'

scenes.description: A transmission pylon seen from directly beneath, geometry filling the frame. Chip reads GERİLİM FARKI.
scenes.on_screen_text: GERİLİM FARKI / 'Elektrik gerilim farkı olan iki'

scenes.description: Close-up of a sparrow on a branch, with a small vector diagram drawn over the footage: two yellow dots joined by a line, each labelled AYNI SEVİYE.
scenes.on_screen_text: 'Kuşun iki ayağı aynı telde,' + AYNI SEVİYE / AYNI SEVİYE

scenes.description: Birds silhouetted on a wire against pale sky, with a yellow rule drawn along the wire. Chip reads AKIM TELDE KALIR.
scenes.on_screen_text: AKIM TELDE KALIR / 'Bu yüzden akım vücudundan geçmez.'

scenes.description: A wooden pole against dramatic cloud, with a red-orange arrow drawn down the wire and a yellow dashed line. Chip is red-orange here, the only time: FARK OLUŞUR · İKİNCİ TEMAS.
scenes.on_screen_text: FARK OLUŞUR · İKİNCİ TEMAS / 'da topraklı direğe dokunursa fark'

scenes.description: The only full-graphic beat: pale cream ground, a flat silhouette of wires and a small bird, and the sentence set large in a dark pill with a yellow underline. No photography.
A cormorant on a wire, sky behind. Closing beat of the first short.
Recording scrolls; the second short begins. Framing changes: footage now sits inside a white rounded frame rather than full-bleed.
Split composition: a drawn wind turbine above a waterline, sand-coloured seabed below, with a vertical scale down the right margin.
A dock crane over water with an orange arc drawn along the lifting cable. Chip reads AĞIR KALDIRMA.
Industrial rig at dusk with an orange cable route drawn over it. Chip reads KABLO ROTASI · ELEKTRİK AKIŞI.
scenes.on_screen_text: KABLO ROTASI / ELEKTRİK AKIŞI / 'Denizin altındaki kablolar elektriği'

scenes.description: A floating platform drawn over sea and sky, mooring lines in orange running down to the seabed. Chip reads YÜZER PLATFORM.

color_palette.overall_mood: Clean, editorial, high-contrast. The photography supplies the colour; the graphics supply exactly two - a yellow for emphasis and a red-orange reserved for the moment of danger or flow.

style_profile.typography_observed: A single humanist sans throughout. Captions in sentence case at medium weight; chips in small uppercase with wide letterspacing; the statement card in heavy uppercase.
style_profile.music_style: Not assessable from the recording - the phone was playing the host video's own audio over it

narration_style.delivery_style: Turkish, calm and even, closely matched to the caption chunks

style_profile.subtitle_style: Burned in, bottom-centre, on a dark rounded pill with generous padding. One word per chunk is set in yellow - the load-bearing word of that line, not a random highlight. Two lines maximum. Sits roughly 15% up from the bottom edge, clear of platform furniture.
style_profile.playbook_delta: No preset matches. It is a stock-footage bed with a persistent two-element HUD (top-left chip, bottom caption pill) plus per-scene vector annotation drawn onto the photograph.

key_elements_to_replicate: Real photographic footage as the bed for most scenes, full-bleed vertical
A persistent HUD: a small uppercase chip top-left naming the current idea, and a caption pill bottom-centre
Exactly one accent colour for emphasis and one reserved for the turning point - and the reserved colour used once
Vector annotation drawn ON the photograph: dots, rules, arrows, dashed leaders that point at the thing being described
One full-graphic statement card at the climax, breaking from photography entirely
A cut roughly every 4 to 5 seconds
One highlighted word per caption line, chosen as the load-bearing word
elements_requiring_custom_work: The annotation layer - the arrows and dots are authored per shot to match what is in that particular photograph, and cannot be templated
Choosing footage where the annotation has something real to point at; a generic pretty clip defeats the whole device
creative_differentiation_seeds: Their chip is a rounded dark pill; ours could be a rule-and-label in the margin, or a struck ledger line - the function is 'name the current idea', the form is ours
They highlight one word in yellow; we could instead set the load-bearing word in a different weight, or let the annotation colour spill into the caption
They cut on a steady 4-5s metronome; a deliberate long hold on the climax would read as ours rather than theirs
Their statement card is cream with a flat silhouette; ours should come out of our own art direction for that piece, not theirs

playbook_customizations.annotation_colour_policy: one emphasis colour, one reserved colour used exactly once
